page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.26xlarge is a high-density compute-optimized server instance belonging to the ecs.c6 instance family. Powered by KVM hypervisors on x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor offering 104 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a ratio of 1.85 GB per vCPU. It does not include local disk storage, requiring external block storage volumes for persistence, nor does it provide discrete GPU accelerators. Networking performance includes a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps, while zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The allocation of 104 vCPUs with 192.0 GB of memory establishes a lean memory-to-CPU ratio tailored for CPU-bound computation rather than memory-heavy operations. The high core count provides extensive parallel processing capabilities, delivering strong density for multithreaded workloads while keeping RAM overhead minimal. Due to the lack of bundled local NVMe storage, data management relies entirely on network-attached storage, which shifts I/O throughput dependencies to the 25 Gbps network interface. This architectural balance makes the instance cost-effective for batch processing, web server clusters, compute-heavy simulation tasks, and continuous integration pipelines that demand high core availability without requiring dedicated local disk drives or GPU hardware.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.26xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance in the ecs.c6 family designed for high-density CPU workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it features 104 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The server contains 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 1.85 GB of memory per core. It omits bundled local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for connectivity and network storage attachment. This allocation profile delivers high parallel processing capacity with low memory overhead per core, maximizing resource density for CPU-bound infrastructure. The configuration is suited for compute-heavy applications such as batch processing, large-scale web serving, code compilation, continuous integration, and mathematical modeling where high vCPU counts are required.
